To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the probability of using internet by respondents who believe on internet service is higher than those who do not believe on internet service; (2) there is significant correlation between belief in internet service and using internet; (3) the probability of respondents to use internet is higher for respondents with high education, high income, young age, and male gender; and (4) the probability of respondent to use internet is also affected by the respondent's belief on internet service.
